text: {"overall_winner": "A", "qualities": [{"evidence": "Essay A acknowledges counterarguments ('Though there are many cons of the driverless car...') and then responds to them, while Essay B only states its own fears without engaging opposing views.", "quality": "Counterargument consideration", "description": "The essay acknowledges and addresses opposing viewpoints rather than presenting a one-sided case."}, {"evidence": "Essay A draws on article details such as cars that 'can steer, accelerate, and break all by themselves' and 'faster reaction time than humans,' whereas Essay B's claims (viruses, hacking) are not grounded in the source text.", "quality": "Use of source evidence", "description": "The essay supports its position with specific details from the article rather than relying on unsupported speculation."}, {"evidence": "Essay A presents a balanced structure weighing pros and cons before reaching a measured conclusion ('could ultimately be a huge success or just a waste of time and money'), while Essay B repeats the same point about distrust throughout.", "quality": "Argumentative development", "description": "The essay builds and advances its reasoning across introduction, body, and conclusion rather than restating a single idea."}, {"evidence": "Essay A frames the debate in terms of societal impact ('decrease the number of speeding tickets, DUI's, and accidents'), while Essay B focuses narrowly on personal distrust and hypothetical hacking.", "quality": "Broader perspective", "description": "The essay situates the argument within wider social consequences rather than only personal opinion."}, {"evidence": "Essay A's prose is more controlled and organized with clear topic progression, whereas Essay B contains informal phrasing and tangents like 'People won't know the fault until they try it.'", "quality": "Clarity and organization", "description": "The essay presents ideas in a coherent, structured manner that makes the argument easier to follow."}]}
